lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Read 25,600 kg of recycling in words and name a sensible comparison (more/less than 20,000 kg).

FEEDBACK
Twenty-five thousand six hundred kilograms; more than 20,000 kg.

WATCH FOR
Dropping units makes a correct digit string less useful in context.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Find or invent eight real-world large numbers. Write each in words with units and one comparison sentence.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
A sign “Crowd 18,450” means eighteen thousand four hundred fifty people, not 18450 without meaning. Place value still structures the digits.

TRY FIRST
Read 25,600 kg of recycling in words and name a sensible comparison (more/less than 20,000 kg).

FEEDBACK
Twenty-five thousand six hundred kilograms; more than 20,000 kg.
teach_steps.explain:
Reading large numbers in context means matching the digits to a real quantity and stating units (people, dollars, grams) with the value.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Dropping units makes a correct digit string less useful in context. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
